summary: Which tool names each supported host binding actually provides, so an agent definition cannot declare a capability the invocation will not grant. A tool name in .claude/agents frontmatter is a claim about the host, and this file is what that claim is graded against.
note: Declaring a tool here does not grant it. A host may still withhold a tool the repository expects; that is a capability the invocation did not grant, never a rule Soveraeign made (CLAUDE.md, Host facts). This contract only refuses the inverse error: naming a tool no supported host provides at all.

claude-code.description: Claude Code, any platform. The tool surface is the harness's, not the operating system's.

portable_note: An agent definition under .claude/agents/ is loaded on whatever host the invocation runs. It may name only portable tools. A shell is reached through Bash on every supported platform; PowerShell was named here until 2026-09-08 and was never a Claude Code tool name on any platform, which is why four agent definitions declared a capability no invocation could grant.

retired.PowerShell: Removed 2026-09-08. Named in four agent definitions and in the CLAUDE.md host-facts section as though it were a Claude Code tool. It is a Windows shell, reached like any other shell through Bash; it is not a tool name the harness resolves.
